request.name: Brittany Spears
request.title: Singer
request.about:
Britney Jean Spears (born December 2, 1981) is an American singer. Often referred to as the "Princess of Pop", she has sold over 150 million records worldwide, making her one of the world's best-selling music artists. An influential figure in popular music, Spears became the best-selling teenage artist of all time, credited with the revival of teen pop during the late 1990s and early 2000s.

Spears began her professional career in 1992 as a cast member of The All-New Mickey Mouse Club and signed with Jive Records five years later. Her first two studio albums, ...Baby One More Time (1999) and Oops!... I Did It Again (2000), are among the best-selling albums of all time. She adopted a more mature and provocative style for her albums Britney (2001) and In the Zone (2003). Spears was the executive producer of her fifth studio album, Blackout (2007), often referred to as her best work. She returned to the top of the U.S. Billboard 200 chart with the albums Circus (2008) and Femme Fatale (2011), and began a concert residency, Britney: Piece of Me (2013–2017), to promote her next two albums, Britney Jean (2013) and Glory (2016). Spears' catalog of high-charting singles includes "...Baby One More Time", "Oops!... I Did It Again", "I'm a Slave 4 U", "Toxic", "Gimme More", "Womanizer", "3", "Hold It Against Me", and "Scream & Shout".

Spears' life, including her high-profile relationships and personal struggles during the 2000s, received widespread media coverage. In 2008, she suffered a mental breakdown and was involuntarily placed in a conservatorship. In 2019, her legal battle over her conservatorship led to the establishment of the #FreeBritney movement and a release of Samantha Stark's documentary Framing Britney Spears (2021). The conservatorship was terminated in 2021, following her public testimony in which she accused her management team and family of abuse. Spears' 2023 memoir, The Woman in Me, reached number one on The New York Times Best Seller list in its first week of release. Her other ventures include starring in the film Crossroads (2002) and launching numerous products, with her 2005 fragrance Fantasy with Elizabeth Arden, Inc. generating over $1.5 billion in sales.

In the United States, Spears is the fourth best-selling female album artist of the Nielsen SoundScan era, as well as the best-selling female album artist of the 2000s. Her accolades include a Grammy Award, 15 Guinness World Records, six MTV Video Music Awards, seven Billboard Music Awards (including the Millennium Award), the Michael Jackson Video Vanguard Award and a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame. Billboard ranked her sixth on their list of the Greatest Pop Stars of the 21st Century. "...Baby One More Time" was named the greatest debut single of all time by Rolling Stone in 2020. Forbes listed Spears as the world's highest-paid female musician in 2001 and 2012. By 2012, she had topped Yahoo!'s list of most searched celebrities seven times in twelve years. Time named Spears one of the 100 most influential people in the world in 2021, placing first in the reader poll.

events.event: Arrested by the California Highway Patrol in Ventura County, California, on suspicion of driving under the influence (DUI) before being released from custody the following morning.
Sold the rights to her extensive music catalog to Primary Wave in a landmark publishing deal reported to be worth approximately $200 million.
Officially announced her permanent departure from the commercial music recording and touring industry.
Filed for divorce from her husband, Sam Asghari, after 14 months of marriage, citing irreconcilable differences.
Released her highly anticipated, best-selling raw memoir 'The Woman in Me', detailing her rise to fame, the trauma of her 13-year conservatorship, and personal struggles.
Released the chart-topping collaborative single 'Mind Your Business' with will.i.am.
Made her grand return to mainstream music after six years with the single 'Hold Me Closer', a duet with Elton John that debuted in the top 10 of the Billboard Hot 100.
Married fitness model and actor Sam Asghari in an intimate, star-studded ceremony at her home in Thousand Oaks, California.
A Los Angeles court officially terminated her 13-year-long conservatorship, fully restoring her legal autonomy, personal freedoms, and financial control.
Delivered a powerful, historic virtual testimony to the Los Angeles Superior Court, publicly detailing the abusive conditions, forced medical treatments, and restrictions of her conservatorship.
Indefinitely suspended her second Las Vegas residency, 'Domination', and announced a career hiatus following her father's severe health emergency.
Launched her record-breaking four-year concert residency, 'Britney: Piece of Me', at the Planet Hollywood Resort & Casino in Las Vegas.
Served as a high-profile celebrity judge for the second season of the reality singing competition series 'The X Factor USA'.
Got engaged to her former manager Jason Trawick, though the couple later split in January 2013.
Released her critically acclaimed seventh studio album, 'Femme Fatale', which debuted at number one on the Billboard 200 and spawned hit singles like 'I Wanna Go' and 'Till the World Ends'.
Released her sixth studio album, 'Circus', featuring the worldwide chart-topping number-one single 'Womanizer'.
Placed under a temporary court-ordered conservatorship following a series of highly publicized personal struggles and hospitalizations, with her father, Jamie Spears, appointed as conservator.
Released her deeply personal and critically lauded fifth studio album, 'Blackout', which went on to become widely celebrated as a benchmark pop masterpiece.
Finalized her highly publicized divorce from backup dancer Kevin Federline, securing joint custody arrangement of their two sons.
Gave birth to her second son, Jayden James Federline.
Gave birth to her first son, Sean Preston Federline.
Married dancer Kevin Federline in a surprise ceremony in Studio City, California.
Released her debut signature celebrity fragrance, 'Curious', with Elizabeth Arden, which went on to become one of the most successful perfume launches in history.
Had a lightning-fast Vegas wedding to childhood friend Jason Alexander at the Little White Wedding Chapel, which was annulled just 55 hours later.
Released her provocative fourth studio album, 'In the Zone', featuring the massive global smash hit 'Toxic', which earned her a Grammy Award.
Generated massive pop culture history at the MTV Video Awards by locking lips on stage with Madonna and Christina Aguilera during a live performance.
Confirmed the end of her high-profile, multi-year relationship with pop singer Justin Timberlake.
Starred in her first leading feature film role as Lucy Wagner in the coming-of-age road movie 'Crossroads'.
Released her explosive third studio album, 'Britney', featuring major hits like 'I'm a Slave 4 U' and famously debuted a live albino python during the MTV VMAs.
Released her blockbuster second studio album, 'Oops!... I Did It Again', selling over 1.3 million copies in the US in its first week alone and breaking modern first-week sales records.
Released her iconic global breakout debut single, '...Baby One More Time', shooting straight to number one on the Billboard Hot 100 and transforming her into an overnight global pop phenomenon.
Born as Britney Jean Spears to James Parnell Spears and Lynne Irene Bridges in McComb, Mississippi, United States.
